from backend import BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall
from event_adapter import EventAdapter

SOURCE = """
@population(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Return the population of a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `"2.1M"`

> use: population
[answer] << How many people live in Paris?
= <answer>
"""


class Script:
    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        if not any(m["role"] == "tool" for m in request.messages):
            return Reply(
                text="Let me look that up.",
                tool_calls=(ToolCall("c1", "population", {"city": "Paris"}),),
            )
        return Reply(text="About 2.1 million.")


events: list[object] = []
dispatcher = AgentEventDispatcher(events.append)
runtime = compile_program(parse_program(SOURCE), adapter=EventAdapter(Script(), model="m1"))
try:
    with bind_agent_event_dispatcher(dispatcher):
        assert runtime.run_main() == "About 2.1 million."
finally:
    dispatcher.close()
    asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())

timeline = [
    (event.state,) if isinstance(event, AgentRunStateEvent) else (event.phase, event.content)
    for event in events
    if isinstance(event, (AgentRunStateEvent, AgentMessageEvent))
]
assert timeline == [
    ("started",),
    ("commentary", "Let me look that up."),
    ("final", "About 2.1 million."),
    ("completed",),
], timeline
assert len({event.run_id for event in events}) == 1

items.title: Hooks
items.text: Hooks let a program or its host observe and change a run: edit or refuse the prompt, edit or refuse a tool call, and observe tool results and failures. Kedi owns the handlers, their order, timeouts, and decisions. The adapter provides the points where they run and declares which events it supports.

items.title: Events
items.text:
Event When Handler may Request type user_prompt_submit before the request is assembled continue, deny, or edit the prompt text UserPromptSubmitRequest (content, read-only media) pre_tool_use before a tool runs, after argument validation continue, deny, or edit the arguments PreToolUseRequest (tool_name, tool_call_id, origin, arguments, ...) post_tool_use after a tool returned observe PostToolUseEvent (result) post_tool_use_failure after a tool raised observe PostToolUseFailureEvent (error_type, error_message, interrupted) post_tool_result_failure after a returned result could not be admitted observe PostToolResultFailureEvent

Handlers come from three places, composed in this order: handlers registered on the adapter instance (adapter.on(...)), the profile's > hooks:, and hooks contributed by capabilities that own a tool.

items.title: Declaring Support
items.text:
Kedi refuses a program whose hooks the adapter cannot run, before any model call:

  • capabilities.hooks is None: Agent hooks are not supported by adapter '<shortname>';
  • an event is missing from it: Agent hook events <names> are not supported by adapter '<shortname>'.

kedi.agent_adapter.HookCapabilities lists each supported event with a HookEventCapability:

Field Meaning bridge "kedi": Kedi's dispatch functions run the handlers at the adapter's call sites. "native": the backend's own hook system calls into Kedi. origins which tool sources the event covers: kedi (registered tools), mcp, adapter_native, provider_builtin supports_mutation whether an edit decision is applied

HookCapabilities.full(tool_bridge=, tool_origins=) declares all five events (post_tool_result_failure only for kedi tools); HookCapabilities.prompt_only() declares only user_prompt_submit.

items.title: Implementing Hooks
items.text:
Three pieces:

  1. Registration. Inherit kedi.agent_adapter.HookRegistrationMixin and call self._init_hook_registration(hook_handler) in __init__. The mixin provides adapter.on(events) and the snapshot Kedi reads. Kedi reads the profile's hooks from the adapter's active_profile.
  2. The prompt hook. For an adapter based on the mixin, Kedi runs user_prompt_submit itself before assembling a program call, and binds the hook dispatcher for the whole call. Children and direct calls do not go through that path, so decorate the async entry points with hooked_agent_run: it runs the prompt hooks for such calls and does nothing when Kedi already ran them for the same run.
  3. Tool hooks. Wrap every tool at its call site with with_hook_lifecycle(tool, adapter_shortname=, tool_call_id=) from kedi.agent_adapter.hooks. The wrapper dispatches pre_tool_use, then the tool, then post_tool_use or post_tool_use_failure. A pre_tool_use denial raises HookDeniedError, which the adapter returns to the model like an approval denial.
hooked_adapter.py
from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Any

from kedi.agent_adapter import HookCapabilities, HookRegistrationMixin, ToolSpec
from kedi.agent_adapter.hooks import hooked_agent_run, with_hook_lifecycle

from backend import ToolCall
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class HookedAdapter(HookRegistrationMixin, ChatAdapter):
    capabilities = replace(
        ChatAdapter.capabilities,
        hooks=HookCapabilities.full(tool_bridge="kedi", tool_origins=frozenset({"kedi"})),
    )

    def __init__(self, *args: Any, hook_handler: Any = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._init_hook_registration(hook_handler)

    @hooked_agent_run("prompt")
    async def invoke(self, *, prompt: str, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
        return await super().invoke(prompt=prompt, **kwargs)

    @hooked_agent_run("template")
    async def produce(self, *, template: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        return await super().produce(template=template, **kwargs)

    async def _execute(self, tools: dict[str, ToolSpec], call: ToolCall) -> str:
        tool = tools.get(call.name)
        if tool is not None:
            hooked = with_hook_lifecycle(
                tool, adapter_shortname=self.shortname, tool_call_id=call.id
            )
            tools = {**tools, call.name: hooked}
        return await super()._execute(tools, call)

HookRegistrationMixin comes first so that its attributes are set up before the adapter's own; it has no __init__ of its own.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
Situation Result a user_prompt_submit handler denies the call fails with HookDeniedError: Kedi hook denied user_prompt_submit: <reason> a pre_tool_use handler denies HookDeniedError; return exc.message to the model, the run continues a handler raises or times out HookExecutionError / HookTimeoutError; propagate, the run fails an edit is not valid for the tool the edited arguments are validated again and rejected like model arguments

Never catch HookExecutionError to continue: a failing hook is a failing safety or audit control.

items.title: Running It
items.text:
run_hooks.py
import asyncio
import json

from kedi.agent_adapter.hooks import PreToolUseDecision, UserPromptSubmitDecision
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall
from hooked_adapter import HookedAdapter

SOURCE = """
@lookup(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Look up a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `"found " + city`

> use: lookup
[answer] << Look up Lyon.
= <answer>
"""


class Script:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.prompts: list[str] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.prompts.append(request.messages[0]["content"])
        results = [json.loads(m["content"]) for m in request.messages if m["role"] == "tool"]
        if not results:
            return Reply(tool_calls=(ToolCall("c1", "lookup", {"city": "Lyon"}),))
        return Reply(text=results[0].get("result") or results[0]["error"])


def run(adapter: HookedAdapter) -> str:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(SOURCE), adapter=adapter)
    try:
        return runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())


observed: list[object] = []
backend = Script()
adapter = HookedAdapter(backend, model="m1")
adapter.on("user_prompt_submit")(
    lambda event: UserPromptSubmitDecision.edit(event.content + " Answer briefly.")
)
adapter.on("pre_tool_use")(lambda event: PreToolUseDecision.edit({"city": "Paris"}))
adapter.on("post_tool_use")(lambda event: observed.append(event.result))

assert run(adapter) == "found Paris"
assert backend.prompts[0] == "Look up Lyon. Answer briefly."
assert observed == ["found Paris"]

refusing = HookedAdapter(Script(), model="m1")
refusing.on("pre_tool_use")(lambda event: PreToolUseDecision.deny("lookups are off"))
assert run(refusing) == "Kedi hook denied pre_tool_use: lookups are off"

items.title: JSON-RPC Bridges
items.text:
Experimental

The protocol is still changing: version 1 gains the capabilities Kedi's in-process adapters have, each in its own message. Until Kedi declares it stable, a release may change it without a compatibility period.

JsonRpcAdapter connects Kedi to a backend written in any language. The backend integration, a bridge, is a process that speaks Kedi's JSON-RPC protocol on its stdio. Kedi renders every piece of text the model reads; the bridge transports it to its framework or harness and calls Kedi's tools back.

The protocol lives in kedi-lang/json-rpc: the specification and a JSON Schema for every message, which Kedi's own tests check its traffic against. This page explains it for bridge authors.

from kedi.agent_adapter import JsonRpcAdapter
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

with JsonRpcAdapter(["node", "my_bridge.mjs"], model="my-model") as adapter:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=adapter)
    runtime.run_main()

From Kedi source, > agent: rpc: with a command: body launches a bridge (see Backend Selection).

The adapter launches the command and owns the process. Readiness is structural: the constructor is the handshake, so an adapter object always has its negotiated capabilities, and a bridge that fails initialize is stopped and never exposed. await JsonRpcAdapter.launch(command) does the same from async code. close() sends shutdown, closes stdin, and stops the process if it has not exited within the timeout.

items.title: Wire Format
items.text:
• JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, UTF-8, at most 8 MiB per line.
  • A line ends at LF (\n) only. Kedi writes U+2028 and U+2029 unescaped, and a text may hold CR. Do not split frames with a reader that also ends lines at those, such as Node's readline or Python's str.splitlines(): split on \n yourself.
  • stdout carries only protocol frames. Write logs and diagnostics to stderr; Kedi drains it and quotes its last lines when the connection fails.
  • A line that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 object, or a line over the limit, ends the connection: every waiting call fails with JsonRpcDisconnected. A disconnected adapter refuses further calls; version 1 has no reconnect, so create a new adapter.
  • Exit when stdin closes, so a bridge never outlives the Kedi process that owns it.

items.title: Methods
items.text:
Method Direction Params Result initialize Kedi → bridge protocolVersion, client, optional testModel protocolVersion, backend (name, version), kind, capabilities, mediaKinds, settings, effort, mcp; see Settings, Effort and Fallback and MCP Servers run Kedi → bridge see below {"text": ...}, {"data": ...} or {"content": [...]}, optional usage, and state in a session run/cancel Kedi → bridge (notification) runId — run/input Kedi → bridge runId, items (id, text) {"delivered": true} or {"delivered": false}; see Live Input and Interrupts run/interrupt Kedi → bridge (notification) runId — ; the run answers with -32006 run/usage bridge → Kedi (notification) runId, inputTokens, outputTokens, optional totalTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens — tool/call bridge → Kedi runId, callId, name, arguments {"ok": true, "result": ...} or {"ok": false, "error": ...} budget/admit bridge → Kedi runId, dimension {"admitted": true}, or admitted: false with dimension and reason, and for a run budget limit, consumed and scopeDepth; see Budgets model/complete bridge → Kedi runId, model, system, messages (Kedi's schema), tools, output message: the assistant's message in Kedi's schema; see Test Model history/process bridge → Kedi runId, messages (the conversation so far, in Kedi's schema) messages: what the program's history processor kept; see History Processing media/get bridge → Kedi runId, ref kind, mediaType, and data (base64) or url; see Transcript artifact/admit bridge → Kedi runId, callId, tool, origin, result result: what the model sees, the result itself or Kedi's artifact reference; see MCP Servers hook/invoke bridge → Kedi runId, event, callId, tool, origin, arguments, optional inputSchema, result, error (type, message), interrupted for pre_tool_use: decision (continue, edit with arguments, or deny with reason); otherwise {}; see Hooks approval/request bridge → Kedi runId, tool, arguments, risk, optional callId and description decision (allow, deny or edit), optional reason, and arguments for edit; see Approval run/event bridge → Kedi (notification) runId, type, see Events — shutdown Kedi → bridge {} {}; then Kedi closes stdin

The protocol version is 1. A bridge that answers initialize with another version, an unknown kind (agent-framework or agent-harness), or no backend name is refused, and the process is stopped.

items.title: Capabilities
items.text:
Capability Meaning structuredOutput the bridge answers runs that have an output with data tools the bridge lets its model call the run's tools through tool/call nativeStructuredOutput the backend takes the output schema natively nativeToolCalling the backend takes tool definitions natively events the bridge sends run/event notifications mediaInput the bridge sends prompt media to its model; mediaKinds lists the kinds (image, audio, video, document) sessions the bridge continues conversations from the state Kedi hands back; enables > history: enabled transcript Kedi holds the conversation in its own schema; runs carry history, results return the turn's messages; enables > history: enabled and history_replay (see Transcript) governed every model request the backend makes goes through budget/admit first; enables request_limit (see Budgets) nativeTools the backend runs tools of its own besides Kedi's, and asks approval/request before each call (see Approval) subagents Kedi may run its children on the bridge (see Subagents); needs governed liveInput the bridge takes input for a running run with run/input; needs subagents interrupt the bridge stops an attempt on run/interrupt; needs liveInput usage the bridge sends run/usage for every model request; enables token_usage, so children can have token limits modelFallback the bridge tries fallbackModels in order when a model request fails; enables > fallback: imageOutput the bridge's model draws images for [img: Image] << ...; see Media Output audioOutput the bridge's model speaks for [speech: Audio] << ...

initialize may also return compaction: {threshold}: the backend compacts its session natively, as a harness does when its context fills up. It needs sessions, and enables compaction_mode: native (see Compaction). threshold says whether the bridge honors an exact input-token threshold.

initialize may also return codemode: {language}: the backend has a code mode of its own, where the model writes python or javascript that calls tools. It needs tools, and makes > codemode: enabled run the backend's code mode (see Code Mode).

Advertise what the bridge implements, not everything its SDK could do. A capability left out is unavailable, and Kedi refuses an operation that needs it before sending anything.

Without nativeStructuredOutput or nativeToolCalling, Kedi adds its protocol.output and protocol.tools parts to the system text (see Rendered Request), and the model answers with JSON actions the bridge parses.

items.title: run
items.text:
Field Contents runId the run; tool/call names it callKind, promptKind invoke or produce; raw, template or claim model the profile's model, or the adapter's default fallbackModels the profile's > fallback: models, in order; empty for none settings the profile's > settings: the bridge listed in initialize, as name and value effort the profile's > effort: level, or null hooks the tool events that have handlers, for a bridge with nativeTools: send hook/invoke for these only (see Hooks); empty otherwise mcpServers the profile's > mcp: servers: transport, command, args, env, url, headers admitResults for a bridge with nativeTools: whether each of its tools' results goes through artifact/admit before the model sees it system the system text: send it verbatim as the system or developer message instructionParts the same text as parts, each with identity, source and content user the prompt: send it verbatim as the user turn userContent null, or the user turn with its media; see Media output null for text; schema (the output JSON Schema) and toolName for data; or media for an image or speech the model makes (see Media Output) tools each tool's name, description, inputSchema, outputSchema and requiredBeforeOutput continuation null, or answer (the bridge's previous result) and message (Kedi's correction) session null, or id, turn and state; see Sessions compaction with a session, when the bridge declared compaction and the profile sets compaction_mode: mode and threshold; see Compaction codemode true when the bridge declared codemode and the profile sets > codemode: enabled; absent otherwise; see Code Mode history in transcript mode, the conversation's earlier messages in Kedi's schema; absent otherwise processHistory in transcript mode, whether the program has a history processor: ask history/process before each model request subagent null, or the child Kedi runs: id, parentRunId, conversationId, name, limits; see Subagents

Kedi validates every answer. When the data does not match the schema, a required tool did not complete, or the bridge reports {"invalid": "<model text>", "error": "<parse error>"}, Kedi sends the same run again with a continuation: replay answer as the model's turn and send message as the next user turn. The bridge never writes correction text and never infers required tools from the prompt. output_retries (default 1) bounds the corrections.

Report usage with the counts the backend measured: requests, inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens. A token count the bridge leaves out is unknown, not zero, and a run without usage has unknown counts; a missing requests is one.

With usage, send run/usage as each model request completes, with that request's counts. Kedi checks a child's token limits as each report arrives, so a limit stops the child after the request that crosses it, as in-process. The run's usage is then ignored. A governed bridge's requests are counted at budget/admit, so run/usage carries tokens only.

items.title: tool/call
items.text: A bridge may call only the tools of a run in progress, with that run's runId. Kedi validates the arguments, applies the approval policy, runs the tool and answers. A failure the model can act on, such as a wrong argument or a denied approval, comes back as {"ok": false, "error": ...} for the model to read. A failure that is not the model's to correct, such as an exhausted budget, stops the run: Kedi answers the call with -32002, sends run/cancel, and raises it. A call still running when its run ends is answered with -32003. Calls run concurrently on the run's event loop, so a tool may itself start a nested run on the same bridge while the outer run waits.

items.title: Media Output
items.text:
With imageOutput, [img: Image] << Draw a cat. reaches the bridge with output {"media": "image"}. Have the model draw, and answer with its content: the parts it made, in the layout of userContent, such as [{"type": "text", "text": "Here it is."}, {"type": "media", "kind": "image", "mediaType": "image/png", "data": "<base64>"}], or a url instead of data. Kedi takes the one image part. When the request holds images, or a tool may return one, output also has schema and toolName: the model may then name one of the request's images instead, and the bridge answers {"data": "<name>"}. Kedi resolves the name to that image, as it does for any media-typed value a model writes.

With audioOutput, [speech: Audio] << Read this aloud. reaches the bridge with output {"media": "audio", "voice": ...}: voice is the profile's > settings: voice, or null for the model's own. The run has no tools and no media. Answer with content holding one audio part, for example {"type": "media", "kind": "audio", "mediaType": "audio/wav", "data": "<base64>"}. Kedi fails a run whose content holds no part of the kind asked for, or more than one.

Without the capability, Kedi has the model name a request image for [img: Image] <<, as for any adapter that cannot draw, and refuses [speech: Audio] << before the run.

items.title: Settings, Effort and Fallback
items.text:
A bridge lists in initialize what it applies: settings, the > settings: names it maps to its backend (Kedi's names or names of its own, such as a reasoning_budget), and effort, the > effort: levels it accepts (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Each run then carries the profile's values for those names in settings, and its level in effort.

Kedi applies its own settings (context_limit, media_limit, request_retries, tool_reason, voice) and never sends them; a bridge may not list them. Kedi refuses a setting or level the bridge did not list before the run, so a program never runs with a configuration it did not get.

With modelFallback, a run carries the profile's > fallback: models in fallbackModels. Try them in order, after model, when a model request fails. A governed bridge asks budget/admit before each attempt: a fallback is a request like any other. Without modelFallback, Kedi refuses > fallback:.

items.title: Budgets
items.text:
A run budget stops a step before it starts, so the bridge asks Kedi before each step it takes:

  • dimension: "request" before every request to its model;
  • dimension: "toolAttempt" before each attempt of one of its own tools, with nativeTools.

Kedi charges the step to the budget of the Kedi call that started the run, counts it, and answers {"admitted": true}. When the budget is spent it answers {"admitted": false, ...} with a reason, sends run/cancel, and fails the run with RunBudgetExceeded. The bridge then skips the step and ends the run with an error; if it takes the step anyway, the run still fails. Kedi admits the attempts of its own tools at tool/call, so a bridge never asks for them.

governed is a promise about the whole backend: every model request goes through budget/admit, including SDK retries, tool-loop turns, native subagents and internal calls such as summarization. A path the bridge cannot route that way must be disabled, or the bridge must not advertise governed. This is the bridge's form of Provider Retries Must Be Observable.

Without governed, Kedi refuses request_limit before the run. Without governed, a bridge with nativeTools also cannot enforce tool_attempt_limit, so Kedi refuses it.

items.title: Approval
items.text:
With nativeTools, the bridge asks before each call of one of its own tools:

{"runId": "r1", "callId": "c1", "tool": "shell", "arguments": {"command": "ls"},
 "risk": "mutating", "description": "Run a shell command."}

risk is read_only, mutating or sensitive, as for Kedi tools: Kedi allows read_only calls and applies the run's approval policy to the rest. Without a policy, the call is denied. The answer is allow, deny with a reason for the model, or edit with the arguments to run instead. When the edited arguments are riskier, ask again before running them. A cancelled approval prompt or a failing approval handler stops the run, as for Kedi tools.

Kedi's own tools need no approval/request: Kedi applies the policy at tool/call.

items.title: Hooks
items.text:
Kedi runs a program's hooks on every bridge: user_prompt_submit before the run is assembled, and the tool events around each Kedi tool at tool/call. The bridge needs nothing for these.

A bridge with nativeTools runs tools of its own, so it reports their calls to the program's hooks: that is part of nativeTools, as approval/request is. Each run's hooks lists the tool events that have handlers; for those, send hook/invoke around each call of a bridge tool, with origin adapter_native for the backend's tools or provider_builtin for tools the model provider runs. With no handlers, hooks is empty and nothing is sent.

  1. pre_tool_use with the call's arguments, before approval/request. Kedi answers continue, edit with the arguments to run instead (ask approval for those), or deny with a reason for the model; skip the call then.
  2. After the call, post_tool_use with its result, or post_tool_use_failure with error {type, message} and interrupted when it was cancelled.

A hook that fails or times out stops the run, as for Kedi tools: a failing hook is a failing safety or audit control. Kedi refuses hook/invoke from a bridge without nativeTools.

items.title: MCP Servers
items.text:
A bridge with nativeTools lists in initialize the > mcp: transports it connects, in mcp {"transports": [...]}: stdio, http (streamable HTTP) and sse. Kedi refuses, before the run, a server whose transport the bridge did not list, and every server for a bridge that lists none. Each run carries the profile's servers in mcpServers; connect them for the run, offer their tools to the model, and close them when the run ends.

An MCP tool is the bridge's own tool, so each call goes through the steps a Kedi tool's wrapper takes, in this order:

  1. hook/invoke pre_tool_use with origin mcp, when the run's hooks lists it;
  2. approval/request with origin mcp and risk mutating: a server cannot declare its tools read-only to Kedi;
  3. budget/admit with toolAttempt, for a governed bridge;
  4. the call itself, then hook/invoke post_tool_use or post_tool_use_failure;
  5. artifact/admit with the result, when the run's admitResults is true: send the model the result Kedi returns. For a large result it is an artifact reference, and the model reads the rest with Kedi's artifact tools.

artifact/admit applies to every result of a bridge tool, not only MCP ones. Kedi's tool-attempt budget still refuses profiles with MCP servers, as for every adapter.

items.title: Subagents
items.text:
With subagents, a profile's children run on the bridge: Kedi decides to start one, checks max_agents, depth and concurrency, and sends the child as a run of its own. Background children are runs that overlap their parent's.

subagent says whose run it is:

Field Contents id Kedi's run id for the child; delegate_task returns it to the parent parentRunId the bridge run whose tool/call started the child, or null conversationId the child conversation; continue_subagent continues it name the child profile limits the child's remaining requests, toolCalls, inputTokens, outputTokens and totalTokens; null for no limit

Kedi enforces the limits; the bridge may pass them to its backend as well, for an earlier stop. Kedi counts each request it admits with budget/admit and each tool call it serves, so a child's request or tool-call limit stops the step before the bridge takes it: budget/admit answers admitted: false with the limit in reason, and a tool/call fails. For a governed bridge, requests in usage is ignored, because Kedi has already counted them. This is why subagents needs governed.

A child sees exactly its own tools. Kedi applies the child's approval policy and every ancestor's to Kedi tools; for the bridge's own tools, approval/request answers with the same policies, ancestors first.

A structured child result has output.schema, the child's result schema with task_summary and final_result. Kedi validates the answer and sends its correction as a continuation, as for any run.

With sessions, continue_subagent sends the state the bridge returned for the child's last completed run, in session with the child's conversationId; Kedi commits it only after accepting the run. Without sessions, the new task carries the earlier turns as text.

items.title: Live Input and Interrupts
items.text:
With liveInput, a parent's send_subagent_input and a child's send_parent_message reach a run while it is running. Kedi sends run/input with each item's text, Kedi's rendering of the message. Add each text as a user turn before the next model request, and answer {"delivered": true} once a model request carries it. Answer {"delivered": false} if the run ends first: Kedi then starts another attempt of the same task with the input in its prompt, and counts that input delivered when the attempt's first request is admitted.

With interrupt, send_subagent_input with interrupt: true stops the child's current attempt. Kedi sends run/interrupt; stop the backend's turn and answer the run with -32006. In a session, put the conversation so far in the error's data as {"state": ...}: the next attempt, with the new input, resumes from it. An interrupt is not a cancel: the task goes on.

items.title: Events
items.text:
With events, a bridge reports what its model writes during a run, and Kedi publishes it to its event observers (see Events, Streaming, and Telemetry) under the Kedi run it belongs to:

type Fields Meaning message.delta messageId, text, optional phase a chunk of a message message.completed messageId, optional text and phase the message is complete; text replaces the chunks tool.boundary — the model called a tool: messages so far are commentary

phase is commentary or final. Kedi starts and ends the run itself, and publishes the run's answer as its final message, so a bridge reports only what the model wrote along the way. Events arrive in stream order before the run's answer. Events for a run that is not in progress, of an unknown type, or without the fields above are ignored, as are all events from a bridge that did not negotiate events.

items.title: Sessions
items.text:
With sessions, a run in a conversation (> history: enabled) carries session: the conversation's id, the turn number, and the state the bridge returned for the conversation's last committed turn, null at first. The bridge answers with the new state, any JSON value: the turn's messages in the backend's own format, a remote thread id, or both.

Kedi owns the conversation: it orders the turns, commits state only after it accepts the turn's answer, discards it after a failed or cancelled turn, and persists it with interactive sessions and snapshots. The bridge keeps no history of its own outside state, so the two sides never disagree. A turn with another model, tools or settings is another lane (see Conversations and History) and starts from null.

state travels in every run, so it counts against the 8 MiB frame. Keep large values, such as media the conversation already sent, out of it: store an id the backend can resolve instead of the bytes. A run whose frame would exceed the limit fails with -32600 before it is sent.

items.title: Compaction
items.text:
A bridge that declared compaction gets the program's policy with each session run: compaction: {mode, threshold}.

  • native. Compact the session as the backend does. When threshold is set, compact once the context reaches that many input tokens. The answer's state is then the compacted session.
  • disabled, or no compaction field. Keep the backend's automatic compaction off, so existing programs see no new requests.

A summary request is a model request like any other. With governed it goes through budget/admit, and with usage it reports run/usage. In test mode it reaches Kedi as model/complete with purpose: "compaction". It is not a turn of the run, so no run/event reports it, and it never carries live input.

Kedi refuses before any model request: - a threshold when the bridge declared threshold: false, as it does for Claude; - native compaction in a program that processes or replays history. Kedi holds that program's transcript, so the bridge has no session to compact.

items.title: Code Mode
items.text:
Kedi's CodeMode does not run on a bridge. A bridge whose backend has a code mode of its own declares codemode: {language}, and > codemode: enabled turns that one on: the run carries codemode: true. The bridge then:

  • turns its backend's code mode on for the run, and offers Kedi's tools to the model's code only, not as tools of their own;
  • sends each call the code makes as it would a direct one: Kedi's tools through tool/call, its own through hooks, approval and admission;
  • gives the code no file, process, network or environment of the machine except through those tools.

Without codemode, or with > codemode: disabled, the backend's code mode stays off. The codemode fixture checks that Kedi's tools are not offered to the model directly.

Kedi refuses, before any model request: - > codemode: enabled on a bridge that declared no codemode; - CodeMode settings (search and execution limits, preload_tools). They are Kedi's sandbox's limits, and the backend's sandbox has its own.

The fast-agent bridge runs fast-agent's Python sandbox (exec_sandbox); the pi bridge runs pi's JavaScript codemode tool. Both need Kedi 0.1.8.

items.title: Transcript
items.text:
With transcript, Kedi holds the conversation instead of the bridge. A run in a conversation carries history, the earlier turns' messages, and the bridge answers with messages, this turn's new ones, the user turn included. Kedi checks them against its schema and appends them when it commits the turn, as it commits state. A transcript run that answers without messages fails.

[{"role": "user", "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "Look at "}, {"type": "media", "ref": "photo"}]},
 {"role": "assistant", "parts": [{"type": "toolCall", "id": "c1", "name": "lookup", "arguments": {}}],
  "providerData": {"...": "the bridge's, sent back as given"}},
 {"role": "tool", "parts": [{"type": "toolResult", "id": "c1", "result": "found"}]},
 {"role": "assistant", "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "Done."}]}]
Part Fields text text media ref: the media's name in userContent toolCall id, name, arguments toolResult id, result, optional isError reasoning optional text

providerData is opaque to Kedi: put there what the backend needs back exactly, such as an encrypted reasoning block. Media is named by ref after the turn that attached it, so its bytes are not sent again with each history. A bridge that needs the bytes, for example after a restart, asks media/get with the ref.

Kedi gives each recorded message an id, so two identical messages stay distinct; send messages back with the id they came with.

items.title: History Processing
items.text:
With a > history: processor, a transcript run carries processHistory: true. Before each model request, tool-loop turns included, send history/process with the conversation so far in Kedi's schema: history followed by this turn's messages. Kedi runs the program's processor, as the in-process adapters do before each request, and answers with the messages it kept. Send the model those instead, and continue the turn from them.

The processor may drop or rewrite earlier messages, so such a run answers with transcript, the whole conversation as it stands after the turn, instead of the turn's messages. Kedi stores it as the conversation. A processor that fails fails the run, as in-process. transcript enables history_processing.

A bridge may support both modes. Kedi uses transcript for an agent-framework bridge, and for an agent-harness only when the program needs Kedi's copy of the conversation (> requires: history_replay, history processing); a harness otherwise keeps its own state. history travels in every run, so a long conversation counts against the 8 MiB frame.

items.title: Media
items.text:
With mediaInput, a prompt's media arrives in userContent, laid out as Kedi lays out every multimodal user turn (see Multimodal Input): text parts, and each attachment where its label puts it.

[
  {"type": "text", "text": "<attachments>\n<image id=\"chart\" type=\"image/png\">"},
  {"type": "media", "name": "chart", "kind": "image", "mediaType": "image/png", "data": "iVBORw0..."},
  {"type": "text", "text": "</image>\n</attachments>\nDescribe chart in one sentence."}
]

data is base64; a media value given by URL arrives as url instead. Send userContent in place of user, each part as the backend's native part. Kedi refuses, before the run, a kind outside mediaKinds and a provider file id, which cannot cross a bridge. A frame holds at most 8 MiB, so send large media by URL.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
Code Meaning -32700…-32603 JSON-RPC parse, request, method, params and internal errors -32001 unsupported: the operation needs a capability that was not negotiated -32002 the run failed in the backend -32003 the run stopped after run/cancel -32004 overloaded: Kedi has no capacity for another request right now -32005 unknown run: the runId names no run in progress -32006 interrupted: the run stopped after run/interrupt; the task continues in another attempt

Kedi admits 64 bridge requests at a time (max_inbound_requests); more are answered with -32004.

When a run fails in the harness, put the harness's own error in the error's data, so the user sees what went wrong behind the bridge:

{"code": -32002, "message": "the harness failed",
 "data": {"harness": {"type": "ProviderError", "message": "429 rate limited",
                      "cause": {"type": "HTTPError", "message": "Too Many Requests"}}}}

Kedi quotes it, with the bridge's last five stderr lines, in the error it raises. When Kedi stops the run itself, for example on an exhausted budget, its own error comes first and the bridge's report follows it:

Kedi error: RuntimeError
  Run request budget exhausted (limit 1, consumed 1)
  from the bridge: the harness failed
  harness error: ProviderError: 429 rate limited
    caused by: HTTPError: Too Many Requests
  bridge stderr:
    [harness] retrying the provider

items.title: Cancellation and Timeouts
items.text: When a Kedi call is cancelled or exceeds request_timeout, Kedi sends run/cancel and stops waiting. The notification is a request: it does not prove that the backend stopped or that side effects were undone.

items.title: Shipping a Bridge as a Package
items.text:
A Kedi package can carry a bridge and give it a shortname. Put the bridge in the package's source tree and declare it as a command:

> package: pi:
  version: 0.1.0
  source: src/pi
  adapters:
    pi:
      kind: agent
      command: node bridge.mjs

After kedi add pi, > import: pi followed by > agent: pi launches node <installed source>/bridge.mjs. The kind must match the bridge's kind: agent for an agent-harness, adapter for an agent-framework. A bridge for a JavaScript harness can be bundled into one file that needs only Node; kedi-lang/json-rpc builds the pi bridge that way.

items.title: Bridge SDKs
items.text:
kedi-lang/json-rpc has a TypeScript SDK (ts/sdk, on npm as @kedi-lang/bridge) and a Python SDK (python/) for writing bridges. They speak the protocol and run the steps Kedi decides around each model request and tool call: admission, live input, history processing, fallbacks, usage, hooks and approval. They also check the bridge in four layers:

Layer When What types compile time (TypeScript) defineHandshake refuses a handshake that breaks the capability rules, such as liveInput without subagents handshake every start the same rules, with Kedi's diagnostic codes (KB001…) preflight first start of each version the conformance fixtures run against the bridge in test mode, for the capabilities it declares runtime while serving the protocol's invariants, such as usage for a request Kedi never admitted, or a step after its run ended

A bridge that fails its preflight answers initialize with the diagnostics, and Kedi's error shows them. --check prints the report; --check --diagnostics json prints it as JSON.

items.title: Reference Bridge
items.text:
kedi.agent_adapter.adapters.jsonrpc.REFERENCE_BRIDGE is a bridge for any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, built with the TypeScript SDK. Kedi ships it bundled into one file that needs only Node.js 20 or later; its source is ts/reference in kedi-lang/json-rpc:

from kedi.agent_adapter.adapters.jsonrpc import reference_bridge_command

adapter = JsonRpcAdapter(reference_bridge_command("http://localhost:11434/v1"), model="llama3")

mode="protocol" uses Kedi's protocol parts instead of native tools and response formats, for endpoints without them. It is governed: it asks budget/admit before every request and makes no retries. It advertises subagents, liveInput, interrupt, usage and transcript: it runs children as ordinary runs, adds live input before its next request, stops a fetch on run/interrupt, and reports each request's token counts. It lists the OpenAI chat settings (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, seed, stop_sequences, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty), sends effort as reasoning_effort, and tries fallbackModels when a request fails. With --image-output it asks image models to draw (OpenRouter's chat completions with modalities image), and with --audio-output audio models to speak (OpenAI's chat completions audio); reference_bridge_command(..., image_output=True, audio_output=True) passes them. In native mode it connects stdio MCP servers for each run, taking each MCP call through the steps above. Start a new bridge from its source.

items.title: Test Model
items.text:
A bridge that declares testModel can have Kedi answer its model requests, for tests with no model endpoint, no network and no cost. Kedi asks for it with testModel: true in initialize; the bridge then sends each model request, admitted as usual, as model/complete instead of calling its model:

Field Content messages the conversation as the model would get it, in Kedi's transcript schema; media may be inline (kind, mediaType, data or url) system the system text the bridge sends its model tools the tools the model may call: name, description, inputSchema output schema and toolName for a structured run, null for text purpose turn, or compaction for the summary request of native compaction

Kedi answers with message, the assistant's reply in Kedi's schema (text, toolCall, reasoning parts), which the bridge treats as its model's. It can also answer with usage: the counts its model would have reported (inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens). That lets a test drive what depends on counts, such as a compaction threshold or a token limit. Without testModel, Kedi refuses a test model at the handshake.

In Python, JsonRpcAdapter(command, test_model=script) takes the script, a function, sync or async, in the style of Pydantic AI's FunctionModel: it receives a ModelCall and returns the assistant's text, or a message with parts, and optionally usage. call.purpose tells a summary request from a turn. Because it sees exactly what the bridge would send its model, a test can check the bridge's prompt, tools and history as well as script its answers:

from kedi.agent_adapter.adapters.jsonrpc import JsonRpcAdapter, ModelCall


def script(call: ModelCall):
    if not any(message["role"] == "tool" for message in call.messages):
        return {"parts": [{"type": "toolCall", "id": "t1", "name": "lookup",
                           "arguments": {"query": "Lyon"}}]}
    return "Found it."


adapter = JsonRpcAdapter(["node", "my_bridge.mjs"], test_model=script)

A harness usually has a scripted model of its own to build this on: pi's @earendil-works/pi-ai faux provider takes a function of the transcript, and a proxy that a bridge runs in front of a harness can answer from Kedi instead of forwarding.

items.title: Conformance
items.text:
kedi adapter check --bridge COMMAND runs the protocol's conformance fixtures against the bridge COMMAND starts: the fixtures the SDKs' preflight runs, shipped with Kedi. The bridge runs in test mode, so it must declare testModel; no model, network or key is involved. Every frame is checked against the protocol's schema, and a fixture whose capabilities the bridge lacks is skipped:

kedi adapter check --bridge "node my_bridge.mjs"

pass  cancel
skip  codemode: the bridge lacks codemode
FAIL  live-input [KB106]: live input does not reach the next model request
      run answered {'code': -32002, 'message': 'KB201: live input arrived, but the run has no run.onInput handler', …}, expected {'text': 'Blue it is.'}
      no run/input answer held {'delivered': True}
      model request 2 did not carry 'Use the blue one.'
      help: register run.onInput and add each text as a user turn; run.modelRequest answers it delivered

--json prints the results as JSON. The command exits 1 when a fixture fails.

kedi adapter check kedi.agent_adapter:JsonRpcAdapter runs the conformance kit against the reference bridge. To check your bridge, give a class a for_conformance(base_url) that launches it with base_url as its model endpoint:

class MyBridge(JsonRpcAdapter):
    @classmethod
    def for_conformance(cls, base_url):
        return cls(["node", "my_bridge.mjs", "--base-url", f"{base_url}/v1"])

The reference bridge passes in both modes:

run_json_rpc_bridge.py
from kedi.agent_adapter import JsonRpcAdapter
from kedi.agent_adapter.adapters.jsonrpc import reference_bridge_command
from kedi.agent_adapter.conformance import check_adapter

for mode in ("native", "protocol"):
    report = check_adapter(
        lambda base_url: JsonRpcAdapter(reference_bridge_command(f"{base_url}/v1", mode=mode))
    )
    assert report.passed, report.render()
    assert report.harness_text == []

items.title: MCP, Skills, and Capability Tools
items.text: Three profile features add tools beyond the program's own procedures. Two of them, skills and eager capabilities, Kedi resolves completely; the adapter sees ordinary tools and instructions. MCP servers are different: the adapter connects to them, so it takes over the work Kedi's tool wrappers do for registered tools.

items.title: Skills
items.text: > skills: enables project-local skill discovery. Kedi adds the skill tools, read_only and already wrapped like every registered tool, and the skills.instructions part. The adapter needs no skill support beyond tool registration; without it, Kedi refuses the profile with AgentToolOverrideUnsupported: Active adapter does not support skill tool registration.

items.title: Capabilities
items.text:
> capability: name: defines a bundle of instructions, tools, MCP servers, approval, and tool hooks that a profile applies with > use:.

Kind What the adapter sees Capability flag eager (default) the bundle's instructions as capability:<identity> instruction parts, its tools as registered tools whose capability_policy carries the bundle's approval and hooks, its MCP servers in mcp_servers supports_capabilities deferred (defer: true) tools whose deferred_capability names a bundle that the model must activate first supports_deferred_tools

For eager bundles the adapter has nothing to implement: calling the wrapped fn applies the bundle's approval, and with_hook_lifecycle (see Hooks) dispatches its tool hooks. Advertise supports_capabilities=True when the adapter registers tools and runs hooks that way; applying a bundle adds an implicit capabilities requirement, and Kedi refuses it for an adapter without the flag.

Deferred activation is a native protocol between Kedi and the framework's own tool loading, implemented today by the Pydantic AI adapter only. A custom adapter leaves supports_deferred_tools unset; Kedi then refuses deferred bundles before inference.

items.title: MCP Servers
items.text:
> mcp: adds servers to profile.mcp_servers, a tuple of kedi.agent_profile.McpServerSpec:

Field Meaning transport stdio, sse, or http command, args, env how to start a stdio server url, headers where to reach an sse or http server

An adapter that advertises supports_mcp=True connects every server in the active profile for the call, lists its tools, exposes them to the model, and closes the connections when the call ends. It refuses, in profile_override, any transport it cannot open; an adapter without MCP support refuses every server (see Profiles, Models, and Settings).

MCP tools are not Kedi tools, so nothing wraps them. For each MCP call the adapter must do what the wrapper does for a registered tool:

Step How approve describe the call as a ToolSpec with metadata={"source": "mcp"} and the default risk="mutating", and apply the policies: request.approval_ceiling inside a child, then tool_approval_policy(spec, profile.approval) hooks with_hook_lifecycle(spec, adapter_shortname=, origin="mcp", tool_call_id=) artifacts admit_current_artifact_result(result, tool_name=, call_id=) before the result reaches the model, and advertise supports_native_artifacts usage MCP calls are invisible to Kedi's tool-attempt budget, which Kedi refuses for profiles with MCP servers

A server's tool cannot declare itself read-only to Kedi: an MCP tool is mutating unless the adapter has a trusted reason to classify it otherwise.

mcp_tools.py
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence
from typing import Any

from kedi.agent_adapter import ToolSpec
from kedi.agent_adapter.approvals.policy import ApprovalPolicy
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.execution import with_approval
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.specs import tool_approval_policy


def mcp_tool_spec(
    *,
    name: str,
    description: str,
    input_schema: dict[str, Any],
    call: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[Any]],
    profile_approval: ApprovalPolicy | None,
    approval_ceiling: Sequence[ApprovalPolicy | None],
    adapter_shortname: str,
) -> ToolSpec:
    """An MCP tool wrapped with the same approval chain as a registered tool."""

    async def run(**arguments: Any) -> Any:
        return await call(arguments)

    spec = ToolSpec(
        fn=run,
        name=name,
        description=description,
        json_schema=input_schema,
        metadata={"source": "mcp"},
    )
    local = tool_approval_policy(spec, profile_approval)
    for policy in reversed((*approval_ceiling, local)):
        spec = with_approval(spec, policy=policy, adapter_shortname=adapter_shortname)
    return spec

items.title: Running It
items.text:
run_mcp_and_skills.py
import asyncio
from dataclasses import replace

from kedi.agent_adapter.approvals.policy import ApprovalPolicy, ToolApprovalDenied
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter
from mcp_tools import mcp_tool_spec


class CapabilityAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    capabilities = replace(ChatAdapter.capabilities, supports_capabilities=True)


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return Reply(text="ok")


SOURCE = """
@lookup(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Look up a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `city`

> capability: evidence:
    > instructions: Cite the supplied evidence.
    > use: lookup

> use: evidence
[answer] << Is Paris the capital of France?
= <answer>
"""

backend = Recorder()
runtime = compile_program(parse_program(SOURCE), adapter=CapabilityAdapter(backend, model="m1"))
try:
    assert runtime.run_main() == "ok"
finally:
    asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
[request] = backend.requests
assert "Cite the supplied evidence." in (request.instructions or "")
assert "lookup" in {tool["name"] for tool in request.tools}


calls: list[dict] = []


async def remote_delete(arguments: dict) -> str:
    calls.append(arguments)
    return "deleted"


def delete_tool(profile_approval: ApprovalPolicy | None, ceiling=()):
    return mcp_tool_spec(
        name="delete_page",
        description="Delete a wiki page.",
        input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"page": {"type": "string"}}},
        call=remote_delete,
        profile_approval=profile_approval,
        approval_ceiling=ceiling,
        adapter_shortname="chat",
    )


async def main() -> None:
    assert await delete_tool(ApprovalPolicy.allow()).fn(page="Draft") == "deleted"
    for tool in (delete_tool(None), delete_tool(ApprovalPolicy.allow(), (ApprovalPolicy.deny(),))):
        try:
            await tool.fn(page="Home")
        except ToolApprovalDenied:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("a denied MCP call must not run")


asyncio.run(main())
assert calls == [{"page": "Draft"}]

The capability's instructions and tool reached the adapter like the program's own; the MCP tool ran only when every policy allowed it, and a parent's deny held even though the child allowed the call.

items.title: Multimodal Input
items.text: A prompt can carry images, audio, video, and documents. The program references a value with <<name>>; the prompt text gets the name, and the value travels beside the text as an attachment. Kedi resolves, checks, and names the attachments. The adapter places each one in the user message in its backend's native form.

items.title: How Attachments Arrive
items.text:
Attachments never arrive as keyword arguments; the entry points keep their prompt: str signatures. Take them from the active request with kedi.agent_adapter.request.take_prompt_media():

from kedi.agent_adapter.request import take_prompt_media

attachments = take_prompt_media()

The first native run inside a Kedi call takes the attachments; runs nested in it, such as a tool's own model call or a child, get an empty tuple. That keeps one image from being sent twice. The same attachments are also readable as current_agent_run_request().prompt.media.

Each item is a MediaAttachment:

Field Content name the name the prompt text uses media the Media value: kind (image, audio, video, document), media_type, and one of data (bytes), url, or file_id; size; text for text documents artifact_ref set when the value is already an artifact and the model can read artifacts: send the reference instead of the content is_text, inline_text() text documents and artifact references travel as text elements summary a byte-free description for logs and hooks

items.title: Laying Out the Message
items.text:
All attachments go in the same user message as the prompt, before the text, each labeled with its name. kedi.agent_adapter.request.media.attachment_content(prompt, attachments) produces that layout as a list of text pieces and the binary attachments in their places:

<attachments>
<image id="chart" type="image/png">
  [the image itself, as the backend's image part]
</image>
</attachments>
Describe chart in one sentence.

Turn each str piece into a text part and each MediaAttachment into the backend's native part for its kind: inline bytes (data), a URL, or a provider file id. Text documents and artifact references are already inlined in the text pieces.

items.title: Checks
items.text:
Kedi checks before the call; the program sees each failure as a KediExecutionError whose original is the MediaError:

Condition Error a prompt has attachments and the adapter does not advertise supports_media_input MediaError: Adapter '<shortname>' does not accept media input; Pydantic AI, LangChain, the Claude Agent SDK, Codex, ACP and A2A take prompts with media an attachment is larger than the media_limit setting MediaError: <name>: ... is larger than the media_limit setting a known provider cannot take the attachment's kind, type, or source MediaError naming the attachment

The adapter adds the checks Kedi cannot make: refuse, with MediaError from kedi.media, a kind or source the backend cannot send, before the request. Never drop an attachment silently or describe it in text instead.

In a conversation, history replay must not resend an attachment the backend already holds; send each attachment with the turn that introduced it.

items.title: Running It
items.text:
multimodal_adapter.py
import base64
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Any

from kedi.agent_adapter.request import take_prompt_media
from kedi.agent_adapter.request.media import attachment_content
from kedi.media import MediaError

from backend import Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class MultimodalAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    capabilities = replace(ChatAdapter.capabilities, supports_media_input=True)

    async def _run(
        self,
        *,
        prompt: str,
        instructions: str | None,
        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None,
        history: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] = (),
        max_requests: int | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Reply, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
        attachments = take_prompt_media()
        if not attachments:
            return await super()._run(
                prompt=prompt,
                instructions=instructions,
                output_schema=output_schema,
                history=history,
                max_requests=max_requests,
            )
        parts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for piece in attachment_content(prompt, attachments):
            if isinstance(piece, str):
                parts.append({"type": "text", "text": piece})
                continue
            media = piece.media
            if media.kind != "image" or media.data is None:
                raise MediaError(f"{piece.name}: {self.shortname} sends only inline images")
            data = base64.b64encode(media.data).decode("ascii")
            parts.append({"type": "image", "media_type": media.media_type, "data": data})
        return await super()._run(
            prompt=parts,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # a structured user message
            instructions=instructions,
            output_schema=output_schema,
            history=history,
            max_requests=max_requests,
        )
run_multimodal_input.py
import asyncio

from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program
from kedi.media import MediaError

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter
from multimodal_adapter import MultimodalAdapter

PIXEL = (
    "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mNk"
    "+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
)
SOURCE = f"""
> import: media

[chart: Image] = `image("{PIXEL}")`
[answer] << Describe <<chart>> in one sentence.
= <answer>
"""


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return Reply(text="A single pixel.")


def run(adapter: ChatAdapter) -> object:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(SOURCE), adapter=adapter)
    try:
        return runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())


backend = Recorder()
assert run(MultimodalAdapter(backend, model="m1")) == "A single pixel."
parts = backend.requests[0].messages[0]["content"]
kinds = [part["type"] for part in parts]
assert kinds == ["text", "image", "text"], kinds
assert parts[0]["text"].startswith('<attachments>\n<image id="chart" type="image/png">')
assert parts[1]["media_type"] == "image/png"
assert parts[2]["text"].endswith("Describe chart in one sentence.")

try:
    run(ChatAdapter(Recorder(), model="m1"))
except Exception as error:
    assert isinstance(error.original, MediaError), error
    assert "does not accept media input" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an adapter without supports_media_input must be refused")

The image reached the backend as its own part, labeled by name, before the prompt text; the adapter without the capability was refused before any request.

items.title: Media in Outputs
items.text:
A model never writes media: where its answer holds an Image or another media type, it names one of its request's media, such as chart or <image chart>. To bind the value, validate the model's structured output inside the call with the request's names:

from kedi.agent_adapter.request.media import media_validation_context

value = TypeAdapter(output_type).validate_python(decoded, context=media_validation_context())

media_validation_context() holds the prompt's attachments and the media Kedi's tools returned so far, and in a conversation every media its requests named; pass your own validation context to it to keep its keys. Kedi's tool argument validators use it already. Kedi's own check after produce returns does not resolve names, so an adapter that skips this step refuses every media name.

items.title: Profiles, Models, and Settings
items.text: A program configures each call through its active profile: > model:, > effort:, > settings:, > fallback:, > mcp:, and the profile directives that select tools, approval, history, and children. The adapter sees the profile only if it implements SupportsProfileOverride.

items.title: The Protocol
items.text:
kedi.agent_adapter.meta.SupportsProfileOverride:

from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile

def default_model(self) -> str | None: ...

def profile_override(self, profile: AgentProfile) -> AbstractContextManager[None]: ...
  • default_model() returns the model the adapter uses when the profile sets none. Kedi records it in telemetry and run records.
  • profile_override(profile) applies profile to every call made inside the context and restores the previous profile on exit. Kedi enters it around each call (see Call Lifecycle), and the adapter enters it for a child in subagent_scope (see Subagents). Overrides nest, so keep a stack in a ContextVar, as the reference adapter does.

items.title: Without the Protocol
items.text:
An adapter that does not implement SupportsProfileOverride runs every call with its own configuration. Kedi then refuses, before the call, any profile that sets a model, fallback models, effort, MCP servers, settings, compaction, or CodeMode:

AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported: Active adapter does not support agent profile override
(requested model=..., effort=..., ...)

> instructions:, tools, approval, and children need no override: they reach the adapter as instructions, registered tools, wrapped tools, and delegation tools.

items.title: With the Protocol
items.text:
Once the adapter implements the protocol, Kedi stops refusing profile fields for it. The adapter must refuse every field it cannot honor, in profile_override, with AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported naming the field. Silently ignoring a field runs the program with a configuration it did not ask for.

Profile field Directive Adapter's job model > model: Use it instead of default_model(). Advertise supports_model_override. effort > effort: Map the level to the backend, or refuse it. Advertise supports_effort. settings > settings: Apply the names listed in capabilities.settings; refuse other names except Kedi's own. Advertise supports_settings. fallback_models > fallback: Try the alternatives on transient failures. Advertise supports_model_fallback; Kedi refuses > fallback: otherwise. mcp_servers > mcp: Connect the servers, or refuse them. See MCP, Skills, and Capability Tools. profile instructions > instructions: Nothing: Kedi renders them into the instructions argument. Do not read them from the profile. approval, hooks, history, artifacts, run_budget, compaction, codemode Owned by Kedi; the capability pages say what the adapter must add.

Kedi still checks capability-gated features for every adapter before the call: > requires:, > fallback: (model_fallback), history processors, native compaction, CodeMode, hook events, and tool_reason.

items.title: Effort
items.text: effort is one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (kedi.effort.EffortValue). Map it onto the backend's reasoning control. When the backend has fewer levels, map to the nearest one and document it; Kedi's Pydantic AI adapter maps max to xhigh (kedi.effort.pydantic_effort_value). When the backend has no reasoning control, refuse effort rather than dropping it.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Kedi knows the settings that it and the built-in adapters accept (see the settings inventory). A custom adapter declares the names it applies, from those or of its own, such as a reasoning_budget its backend takes:

capabilities = AdapterCapabilities(
    supports_settings=True,
    settings=frozenset({"temperature", "reasoning_budget"}),
)

Kedi refuses a name the adapter does not declare before the first model request: adapter '<shortname>' does not take the settings <names>.

Five settings belong to Kedi and may appear in any profile (kedi.agent_profile.settings.KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS):

Setting Owner Adapter's job context_limit Kedi's request-size check none media_limit Kedi's media check none request_retries the adapter's request retries read it with request_retry_limit(settings, default) tool_reason approval reasons only adapters that list tool_reason in capabilities.settings may receive it; Kedi refuses it for the others voice speech output an adapter with supports_audio_output reads it with speech_voice(settings)

items.title: Model Fallback
items.text: fallback_models is an ordered tuple of model IDs. Kedi's adapters try the next model when a request to the current one fails with a transient provider error (kedi.agent_adapter.request_retry.transient_provider_error: status 408, 429, or 5xx), per request, after request retries are exhausted. They do not fall back after a response has started streaming, and an alternative never replaces an unresolved primary model.

items.title: Running It
items.text:
run_profiles.py
import asyncio

from kedi.agent_adapter import MissingAdapterCapabilityError
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return Reply(text="ok")


def run(source: str) -> list[BackendRequest]:
    backend = Recorder()
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=ChatAdapter(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
    return backend.requests


[default] = run("[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
assert default.model == "m1"

[fast] = run(
    "> profile: fast:\n"
    "    > model: m-fast\n"
    "    > settings:\n"
    "        temperature: 0.2\n"
    "> use: fast\n"
    "[a] << Hi.\n"
    "= <a>\n"
)
assert fast.model == "m-fast" and fast.temperature == 0.2

for directive, field in (
    ("> effort: high", "effort"),
    ("> settings:\n    max_tokens: 10", "max_tokens"),
):
    try:
        run(f"{directive}\n[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
    except Exception as error:
        assert isinstance(error, AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported) or isinstance(
            getattr(error, "original", None), AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
        ), error
        assert field in str(error)
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"{field} must be refused")

try:
    run("> model: m1\n> fallback: m2\n[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
except Exception as error:
    assert "model_fallback" in str(error), error
    assert isinstance(error, MissingAdapterCapabilityError) or isinstance(
        getattr(error, "original", None), MissingAdapterCapabilityError
    )
else:
    raise AssertionError("fallback needs supports_model_fallback")

items.title: Prompts and Instructions
items.text: Kedi writes every piece of text a model reads for a Kedi call. The adapter sends that text to its backend unchanged. This page lists what the text contains, in which order, and the few places where an adapter influences it.

items.title: The Two Strings
items.text:
Each call carries two strings:

Argument Send it as Contents instructions the system or developer message instruction parts, joined in order with a blank line prompt (invoke) / template (produce) the user message the rendered prompt for this call

Send each exactly once. Do not parse them, re-render them, translate them into another format, or add text of your own around them.

items.title: Instruction Parts
items.text:
instructions is built from parts. Each has a stable identity and a source, and appears only when it applies:

Order Identity Source Present when 1 template.instructions runtime the call is a template capture in completion mode; wrapped in <TemplateInstructions> 2 profile.instructions profile the profile has > instructions: 3 capability:<identity> capability an active capability contributes instructions 4 grounding.instructions runtime the profile has tools, MCP servers, or skills; wrapped in <ToolCallInstructions> 5 skills.instructions skills skills are enabled 6 artifacts.instructions artifacts the artifact contract is active for the call 7 runtime.claim runtime the call is a claim 8 media_output.instructions runtime the output or a tool's parameters take media, and the call attaches media or offers tools; wrapped in <MediaOutputInstructions>

Two consequences for adapters:

  • The text is cache-stable. Parts are ordered from the most stable to the most call-specific, and their content does not change between calls with the same profile and tools. Keep instructions first in the provider request so prompt caching works.
  • Profile instructions are already included. Do not also read the profile's > instructions: from the active profile and send them; they would appear twice.

items.title: The Prompt
items.text:
Call Prompt raw invoke << the rendered text of the statement template capture, completion mode Fields to be substituted into the template string for final construction: (a, b). followed by The template string: and the rendered template template capture, decision mode Evaluate each marked decision field using its question, criteria, and the context below. followed by the field list and the rendered template as context claim Claim: <rendered claim> child run the delegated task; see Subagents

The completion rules (what a field value is, how to treat the surrounding template text, escaped brackets, and so on) live in <TemplateInstructions>, not in the prompt. Models that should not receive them, such as a classifier, use decision mode.

items.title: Decision Mode
items.text:
An adapter chooses the template prompt mode per profile by implementing SupportsTemplatePromptMode:

from kedi.agent_adapter.meta import TemplatePromptMode
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile

def template_prompt_mode(self, profile: AgentProfile) -> TemplatePromptMode:
    return "completion"  # or "decision"

In decision mode the prompt asks the model to evaluate each field from the context, and template.instructions is left out. Kedi's decision models (TypeSafe Jev and Laya) use it. Adapters for general chat models do not implement the protocol and get completion mode.

items.title: Hook Edits
items.text: user_prompt_submit hooks run before the request is assembled. When a hook replaces the prompt, the adapter receives the replaced text, and so do telemetry, budgeting, cache identity, and history. The adapter must not apply hooks again or keep a copy of the original prompt. See Hooks.

items.title: What an Adapter Must Not Add
items.text:
• template-filling or field-extraction rules, examples, or reminders;
  • output-format instructions such as "answer in JSON with fields ...": send the JSON Schema through the backend's structured-output feature instead (see Structured Output). A backend without one declares supports_native_structured_output=False, and Kedi renders the output contract as the protocol.output part (see Rendered Request);
  • tool-usage instructions or tool catalogs: declare supports_native_tool_calling=False instead, and Kedi renders them as the protocol.tools part;
  • a second copy of the profile instructions or of any part above;
  • correction turns of its own. Send Kedi's: output_correction, required_tools_correction and protocol_correction, or the text accept_subagent_output gives for child results.

Text that identifies a harness and does not depend on the request, such as an agent harness's own fixed system prompt, is not part of this contract.

items.title: Seeing the Text
items.text:
run_prompt_contract.py
import asyncio
from typing import Any

from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self, reply: Reply) -> None:
        self.reply = reply
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return self.reply


def run(source: str, reply: Reply, adapter_type: type[ChatAdapter] = ChatAdapter) -> BackendRequest:
    backend = Recorder(reply)
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=adapter_type(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
    [request] = backend.requests
    return request


PROFILE = """
@lookup(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Look up facts about a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `'facts'`

> instructions: Answer as a careful geographer.
> use: lookup
"""

capture = run(PROFILE + ">> The capital of France is [city].\n", Reply(data={"city": "Paris"}))
system = capture.instructions or ""
order = [
    system.index("<TemplateInstructions>"),
    system.index("Answer as a careful geographer."),
    system.index("<ToolCallInstructions>"),
]
assert order == sorted(order), system
assert capture.messages[0]["content"].startswith(
    "Fields to be substituted into the template string for final construction: (city)."
)
assert system.count("Answer as a careful geographer.") == 1

claim = run(PROFILE + "> if: Paris is in France\n  = yes\n", Reply(data=True))
claim_system = claim.instructions or ""
assert "<TemplateInstructions>" not in claim_system
assert claim_system.index("Answer as a careful") < claim_system.index("Determine whether")
assert claim.messages[0]["content"] == "Claim: Paris is in France"

A decision-mode adapter receives a different prompt and no completion rules:

run_prompt_contract.py
class DecisionAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    def template_prompt_mode(self, profile: Any) -> str:
        return "decision"


decision = run(
    ">> The ticket [urgent: bool] needs a reply today.\n",
    Reply(data={"urgent": True}),
    DecisionAdapter,
)
assert decision.messages[0]["content"].startswith("Evaluate each marked decision field")
assert "<TemplateInstructions>" not in (decision.instructions or "")

items.title: Reference Adapter
items.text:
Every page in this section extends one adapter, ChatAdapter, that connects Kedi to a chat backend with tool calling and JSON Schema output. The code on these pages is complete: the documentation test suite assembles the python title="..." blocks into modules and runs them through real Kedi programs.

The adapter is about 170 lines. It implements:

Protocol or attribute Defined in Section kind, shortname, capabilities kedi.agent_adapter.AgentAdapter Overview invoke, invoke_sync, produce, produce_sync kedi.agent_adapter.AgentAdapter Calls default_model, profile_override kedi.agent_adapter.meta.SupportsProfileOverride Profiles tool_scope, register_tool kedi.agent_adapter.SupportsToolRegistration Tools

Later pages add subagents, conversations, and the other optional protocols to the same class.

items.title: The Backend
items.text:
The backend stands in for your provider SDK. It receives one rendered request and returns one reply: text, a decoded JSON value, or tool calls.

backend.py
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolCall:
    id: str
    name: str
    arguments: dict[str, Any]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reply:
    text: str | None = None
    data: Any = None
    tool_calls: tuple[ToolCall, ...] = ()
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BackendRequest:
    model: str
    instructions: str | None
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
    tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    temperature: float | None = None


class Backend(Protocol):
    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply: ...

A real backend translates BackendRequest into its provider call: instructions becomes the system or developer message, messages the conversation, tools the provider's tool declarations, and output_schema its structured-output or response-format option.

items.title: The Adapter
items.text:
chat_adapter.py
from __future__ import annotations

import inspect
import json
from collections.abc import Generator, Sequence
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from typing import Any

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic_core import to_jsonable_python

from kedi.agent_adapter import AdapterCapabilities, AgentAdapterKind, HookDeniedError, ToolSpec
from kedi.agent_adapter.approvals.policy import ToolApprovalDenied
from kedi.agent_adapter.execution import run_sync
from kedi.agent_adapter.invocation import InvocationUsage, report_invocation
from kedi.agent_adapter.output_schema import build_output_model
from kedi.agent_adapter.request_retry import request_retry_limit, wait_for_request_retry
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.errors import correctable_tool_error
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.execution import validate_tool_arguments
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile, AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
from kedi.agent_profile.settings import KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS
from kedi.run_budget import admit_run_operation

from backend import Backend, BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall


class ChatAdapter:
    kind: AgentAdapterKind = "agent-framework"
    shortname = "chat"
    capabilities = AdapterCapabilities(
        supports_structured_output=True,
        supports_tool_registration=True,
        supports_artifacts=True,
        supports_profile_override=True,
        supports_model_override=True,
        supports_effort=False,
        supports_settings=True,
        settings=frozenset({"temperature"}),
        supports_mcp=False,
        supports_request_budget=True,
        supports_tool_attempt_budget=True,
    )

    def __init__(
        self, backend: Backend, *, model: str, max_steps: int = 8, request_retries: int = 2
    ) -> None:
        self._backend = backend
        self._model = model
        self._max_steps = max_steps
        self._request_retries = request_retries
        self._profiles: ContextVar[tuple[AgentProfile, ...]] = ContextVar(
            f"chat_profiles_{id(self)}", default=()
        )
        self._tools: ContextVar[tuple[ToolSpec, ...]] = ContextVar(
            f"chat_tools_{id(self)}", default=()
        )

The ContextVars give every concurrent call, thread, and subagent its own profile stack and tool set. Kedi runs template blocks in parallel and children in background tasks, so state stored on self would leak between them.
